title: Five Ways to Stay Safer Online as AI Boosts Cyber Threats
excerpt: AI can make scams more convincing, but familiar security habits still offer protection. Here are five steps to reduce your exposure.
author: LokkeeVerse
content:
A vulnerability in PHP, a programming language widely used to power websites, sent businesses and governments scrambling to apply fixes, according to Reuters. The report highlights a broader concern: as artificial intelligence helps attackers work faster and craft more convincing deception, people need practical defenses that protect both their accounts and their everyday browsing.

## Why AI changes the threat

AI can help criminals produce polished phishing messages, translate scams into multiple languages and generate code. That makes poor spelling a less dependable warning sign. A message that sounds professional, familiar or urgent still needs checking, especially if it requests money, login details or an unexpected download.

Software vulnerabilities present a different problem. A flaw in technology used by a website can expose visitors or their information even when they have done nothing wrong. Fixing server-side software such as PHP is generally the responsibility of website operators and hosting providers, not individual visitors.

## Five habits that reduce your risk

The strongest personal defenses combine account protection, prompt updates and a pause before acting on unexpected requests. No single tool can prevent every attack, but several simple measures can make account takeover harder and reduce the damage if a device or service is compromised.

It also helps to distinguish between a genuine security notice and a scam exploiting the headlines. Attackers may impersonate technical support or claim that an urgent patch is required. Reach services through their official apps or a known address rather than following links in unsolicited messages.

- **Update your software.** Enable automatic updates for operating systems, browsers and apps. Website administrators should follow vendor guidance and promptly install applicable security fixes.
- **Strengthen your logins.** Use unique passwords stored in a password manager, and enable passkeys or multifactor authentication wherever available.
- **Verify unusual requests.** Confirm payment demands or requests for sensitive information through a separate, trusted channel, even when the sender sounds familiar.
- **Protect recovery options.** Keep account recovery details current, store backup codes securely and never share one-time authentication codes with someone who contacts you.
- **Back up important files.** Maintain backups separate from your main device, and check that you can restore them if ransomware or another incident strikes.
